name: Tyson Foods, Inc.
sector: Consumer Staples / Protein processing & packaged foods
moat_justification: Scale, distribution, and branded Prepared Foods are real, but most of the sales base is raw commodity protein with little brand or pricing power, so returns are driven by cattle/hog/feed cycles Tyson does not control; beef losses, a $343M beef goodwill impairment, and recurring legal accruals confirm the weak moat.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 13 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
one_liner: Weak-moat (3/10) commodity protein processor — chicken and branded prepared foods are real, but beef-cycle losses and recurring legal accruals cap owner's earnings; at $54.04 it does not clear 15% in any scenario (weighted IRR 8.1%, IV@15% $24.21; hurdle-clearing price $24.21, super-bull IV only $46.85).
moat_for: Largest US meat company by volume; procurement, processing, and distribution scale
Branded Prepared Foods portfolio (Jimmy Dean, Hillshire Farm, Ball Park) with steadier, higher margins
Vertically integrated chicken operations — the current profit engine
Multi-protein diversification — chicken and prepared foods currently offset beef losses
moat_against: Raw beef/pork/chicken are commodities with little to no pricing power; margins set by livestock/feed spreads
Beef cycle exposure structural — multi-decade-low cattle herd, FY2026 beef losses guided wider
Recurring legal contingency accruals ($698M-$738M in FY2025) look systemic, not one-off
Limited synergies across the three proteins; diversification adds complexity
